contentBody: **A page looks expensive but the only button does not open anything. What is true?**
option.1: The prototype is testable because the theme looks complete
option.2: Friends clapping is enough evidence that the offer is understood
option.3: Adding more pages will automatically fix the missing next step
option.4: It is not testable until there is one working next step to use
answerExplanation: A dead call-to-action fails the good-enough gate. Looks do not replace a button or form that actually works.

contentBody: **Planned feedback for an early prototype is organised into which three layers?**
option.1: Understanding of the offer, desire to use it, and where they stall
option.2: Logo, colour palette, and dark mode
option.3: Payments, admin dashboard, and a city-wide launch
option.4: Testimonials, fake star ratings, and investor quotes
answerExplanation: You plan to learn whether people get the offer, whether they want the job done, and where they stall. Decoration and fake social proof are not those layers.

contentBody: **Someone opened the link and completed a small waitlist form. What does that count not prove by itself?**
option.1: That a person looked and that the button could be used
option.2: That they completed the small action you asked for
option.3: That the idea is already a proven, paying business
option.4: That you can later tally a simple yes, maybe, or no
answerExplanation: Opens, form fills, and yes/maybe/no are simple counts about interest in the offer. They are not proof of a company, a market survey, or payment.
